UNDERSTANDING LINEAR INEQUALITIES
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

• Say what understanding linear inequalities means in plain words.
• Give one clear example linked to Linear Inequalities.

INTRODUCTION
----
Understanding Linear Inequalities. Get clear on linear inequalities before moving on. How would you explain linear inequalities to a classmate in one minute? Use this anchor: Apply inequality symbols to inequality statements in learning situations. Clue from the topic: Illustrate simple inequalities. Check every example on this page against that anchor.

MAIN NOTES
----
• An algebraic expression uses numbers and letters (variables) joined by operations.
• Like terms have the same variable part — combine them; unlike terms stay separate.
• To solve an equation, undo operations carefully on both sides.
• Check by substituting your answer back into the original equation.
• Example: if x = 4, then 2x + 7 = 15.
